whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Manufacturing Cloud Accredited Professional exam?

personas.label: Manufacturing implementation consultants
personas.description: You deliver Salesforce solutions for manufacturers and want to demonstrate knowledge of sales agreements, forecasts, and rebate processes.

personas.label: Salesforce administrators in manufacturing
personas.description: You support a Manufacturing Cloud org and want to validate your understanding of account forecasts, demand planning, and partner workflows.

personas.label: Supply chain and ERP integration partners
personas.description: You connect Manufacturing Cloud with ERP systems and need to understand how order, inventory, and pricing data move between platforms.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Manufacturing Cloud AP exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers manufacturing sales operations, including sales agreements, account-based forecasting, rebates, partner management, and ERP integration. Candidates new to manufacturing demand planning may need time to learn these concepts and how they connect.
bullets: 50 scored questions in 75 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
68% to pass, which is 34 correct answers out of 50.
Sales agreements: Understand agreement terms, attainment, and how actual order data is compared with commitments.
Forecasting: Review account forecasts, run rate demand, adjustments, and the relationship between sales plans and operations.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice explaining how a sales agreement supports an account forecast and how actuals are populated. Review partner sales processes and common ERP data flows. Use the current exam guide to confirm exam requirements before booking.

examFormat.heading: Manufacturing Cloud Accredited Professional exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in person. Questions cover manufacturing sales and partner processes.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Some questions describe distributor commitments, account forecasts, rebate programs, or ERP integrations and ask how Manufacturing Cloud should support the process.
bestWayToPass: Review sales agreements: Understand agreement records, terms, planned quantities, actuals, and attainment.
Study account forecasts: Learn forecast periods, metrics, adjustments, and rollups across account hierarchies.
Understand rebates: Review eligibility, tiers, accruals, and how final payouts are determined.
Map ERP integration needs: Identify data ownership, direction, timing, transformation, and failure handling for order and inventory data.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Manufacturing Cloud setup for sales agreements, account-based forecasting, rebate programs, partner management, and ERP integration. The exam is 50 scored questions in 75 minutes, with a 68% pass mark, weighted towards Configure and Build (38%) and Design (28%).

blocks.heading: Sales Agreements and Account Forecasts
blocks.body: A sales agreement records a manufacturer’s negotiated commitments with a distributor or dealer over a defined term. Agreement terms can describe product-level planned quantities and prices for forecast periods. Actual order data can be compared with the planned values to show attainment. Account-based forecasts combine agreement information with other demand signals such as open opportunities and run rate business. Forecast adjustments let authorized users account for changes that are not reflected in the underlying data. Understand how orders link to agreements and how forecast periods roll up.

blocks.heading: Run Rate Business and Demand Planning
blocks.body: Run rate business represents recurring purchases from customers without a formal sales agreement. Historical ordering patterns can help estimate future demand. A combined forecast may include agreement commitments, run rate demand, and other sales inputs. Forecast collaboration helps sales, supply chain, and finance stakeholders review assumptions and adjust plans. Know the difference between contracted agreement demand and recurring demand inferred from customer behavior.

blocks.heading: Partner Visits and Field Execution
blocks.body: Manufacturers may use partner visit processes to support dealer and distributor relationships. Visit plans can organize schedules and objectives. During a visit, a representative may review agreement attainment, discuss planned orders, capture inventory observations, or record competitive information. Action plans can provide repeatable checklists, and assessments can capture structured responses. Confirm how the selected product and licenses support mobile or offline work before designing the process.

blocks.heading: Rebates, Incentives, and Pricing
blocks.body: Rebate programs define the conditions under which a dealer or distributor earns an incentive. Tiers can set different payout rates at different volume thresholds. Accruals estimate the expected liability as eligible sales occur, while the final payout settles the amount due for the program period. Sales agreement prices may reflect negotiated terms. Keep rebate calculations, agreement pricing, and general price book records distinct when assessing a scenario.

blocks.heading: ERP and Supply Chain Integration
blocks.body: ERP systems may own order, inventory, and financial data that Manufacturing Cloud needs for agreement attainment or planning. Define the source of truth for each field and how data moves between systems. Product pricing may also need synchronization. Integration design should account for transformation, volume, timing, errors, and temporary outages. Middleware such as MuleSoft may be used, but the integration approach should be selected for the customer’s architecture and requirements.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Manufacturing Cloud AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: For each scenario, identify whether it concerns a sales commitment, forecast, incentive, partner activity, or ERP data flow. Then determine which records or process support that need.

blocks.heading: Follow Agreement Terms and Actuals
blocks.body: Know how planned product quantities and prices are recorded and how actual order data is compared with those commitments over time.

blocks.heading: Build an Account Forecast
blocks.body: Understand forecast periods, agreement demand, run rate demand, adjustments, and rollups. Check how the forecast will be used by sales and operations.

blocks.heading: Review Rebate Programs
blocks.body: Know how eligibility and tier thresholds affect accruals and payouts. Distinguish an incentive from a change to product list price.

blocks.heading: Support Dealer and Distributor Work
blocks.body: Connect partner visits and account planning to the information representatives need, such as attainment, upcoming orders, and structured assessment results.

blocks.heading: Plan ERP Data Exchange
blocks.body: Define which system owns orders, inventory, and pricing, then specify data direction, transformation, refresh timing, and recovery behavior.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials after Manufacturing Cloud AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on manufacturing implementation work with a Salesforce consultant or integration credential.

sampleQuestions.question: A manufacturer and distributor agree on a product volume and price for the coming year. Which record tracks that commitment?
options: An open opportunity kept active for the full year
A contract description containing the quantity as text
A sales agreement
A new quote for each order
sampleQuestions.explanation: A sales agreement records planned commitments and terms for a distributor or dealer over a defined period.
whyWrong: An opportunity represents potential sales rather than structured commitments over a term.
A description field cannot support product-level planned and actual quantities.
A sales agreement records the negotiated commitment over time.

sampleQuestions.question: What can a sales agreement help a manufacturer compare?
options: Forecasts from separate sales regions
Open customer cases against industry averages
Planned quantities with actual orders
Product list price with manufacturing cost
sampleQuestions.explanation: Agreement terms provide planned quantities that can be compared with actual order data over the term.
whyWrong: Regional forecast comparison is a separate analysis.
Service cases track support work rather than purchase commitments.
Planned quantity compared with actual orders shows agreement attainment.

sampleQuestions.question: A distributor is tracking below its committed volume halfway through the agreement. What is a useful next step?
options: Invoice the distributor for the full shortfall immediately
Open a service case for the sales team
Close the agreement and create a replacement without discussion
Review the agreement with the customer and revise it if appropriate
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reviewing the commitment and customer outlook helps determine whether the agreement or forecast assumptions need to change.
whyWrong: A shortfall does not automatically mean the customer should be billed for the full variance.
A service case is not the usual record for reviewing a volume commitment.
Closing the agreement without review loses the opportunity to understand the variance.

sampleQuestions.question: What does account-based forecasting help a manufacturer understand?
options: Production capacity at each plant
Sales commission owed to each representative
Total pipeline across all company opportunities
Expected volume and revenue for each account over time
sampleQuestions.explanation: Account-based forecasting presents expected volume and revenue by account and forecast period.
whyWrong: Plant capacity is an operations measure, not an account forecast.
Commission is not the purpose of an account forecast.
Total pipeline does not provide expected demand by account over time.

sampleQuestions.question: A manufacturer sells to distributors that then sell to end customers. What capability is important for understanding downstream demand?
options: Visibility into demand beyond the direct customer
Removing all end-customer information from systems
Invoicing every end customer directly
Creating a separate Salesforce org for every distributor
sampleQuestions.explanation: Downstream demand visibility helps a manufacturer understand channel activity beyond its direct distributor orders.
whyWrong: Downstream demand visibility helps manufacturers understand channel sales.
Visibility supports understanding end-market demand rather than removing all related data.
Direct invoicing is not required to receive downstream demand information.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a program in Manufacturing Cloud?
options: Store engineering drawings for product variants
Group customer agreements
Maintain production-line employee training records
Schedule equipment maintenance at each plant
sampleQuestions.explanation: A program can organize related customer agreements and activities around a shared initiative.
whyWrong: Engineering drawings belong in product lifecycle or document management.
A program can group related agreements and activities for an initiative.
Training and maintenance records are separate operations data.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might a manufacturer use rebates alongside sales agreements?
options: To reward a dealer or distributor when volume thresholds are met
To invoice the customer monthly instead of annually
To reduce list price for every customer in the market
To record shipping cost
sampleQuestions.explanation: A rebate can reward qualifying volume or other defined performance during a program period.
whyWrong: Rebates can reward qualifying volume or performance.
Invoice frequency is separate from rebate eligibility.
Rebates do not necessarily change general market list price.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales agreement price should increase starting next quarter. What is an appropriate approach?
options: Change the general price book entry and rewrite all history
Add a note to the account for representatives
Update the agreement terms with the new price and effective period
Delete the agreement and recreate it without history
sampleQuestions.explanation: Updating the relevant agreement terms with an effective date preserves the commitment history and applies the price when intended.
whyWrong: Changing the list price may affect other customers and obscure history.
A note does not update structured agreement pricing.
An effective-dated agreement term can record the new price while retaining history.

sampleQuestions.question: What is needed for a planned-versus-actual agreement view to be useful?
options: Every catalog product has a published list price
Orders are linked to the agreement
The account has an open service case
The sales representative updates the forecast weekly
sampleQuestions.explanation: Order data linked to the agreement can provide actuals for comparison with planned quantities.
whyWrong: Catalog list price does not supply actual order quantities.
Linking orders to the agreement lets the system compare actuals with plan.
Service cases do not populate agreement actuals.

sampleQuestions.question: A manufacturer wants partners to submit their sales data through Salesforce. What can support this?
options: Require partners to use the manufacturer’s internal systems
Ask the account manager to call each partner monthly
Send a spreadsheet by email for monthly completion
Provide a partner community where they can enter data
sampleQuestions.explanation: A configured partner community can provide a controlled place for partners to submit information.
whyWrong: Partners may not be able to use the manufacturer’s internal systems.
Phone collection is difficult to scale and audit.
Email spreadsheets require manual handling and version control.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a key difference between a sales agreement and a contract?
options: A sales agreement tracks planned volumes and actuals over a term
Contracts are only for new customers
Agreements cover services while contracts cover products
Contracts are signed but agreements are never signed
sampleQuestions.explanation: A sales agreement focuses on planned and actual purchase volumes over time.
whyWrong: A sales agreement tracks planned volumes and actuals over a term.
The distinction is not based on whether a customer is new.
Agreements and contracts are not divided by service versus physical goods.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer orders more than the planned quantity in its agreement. What should the agreement’s actuals show?
options: The excess should be placed on a separate agreement automatically
Actuals can exceed the planned quantity
The planned quantity should automatically rise to equal the order
The extra order must be rejected
sampleQuestions.explanation: Actuals record what was ordered, so they can be greater than the planned amount.
whyWrong: A separate agreement is not required merely to record actuals above plan.
Actuals can exceed planned quantities and show a variance.
Planned quantities should not automatically change to hide the variance.

sampleQuestions.question: Why does forecast accuracy matter to manufacturers?
options: Production and materials may need to be committed in advance
Customers cannot order until a forecast is approved
Sales representatives are paid only on forecast accuracy
Regulators require public quarterly forecasts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Manufacturers use forecasts to plan production and materials before demand is fully realized.
whyWrong: Forecasts help manufacturers commit production and materials in advance.
Orders are not generally blocked until a forecast is approved.
Compensation is not universally determined only by forecast accuracy.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a benefit of storing agreements and orders in the same system?
options: It removes the need for finance or billing systems
It automatically gives every customer access to agreement records
Actuals can update against commitments without rekeying
It recalculates prices across the entire catalog
sampleQuestions.explanation: When orders and agreements are connected, actuals can be compared with commitments without manually re-entering data.
whyWrong: CRM does not eliminate the need for separate finance or billing systems.
Customer access requires configuration and is not automatic.
Connected orders can update actuals against agreement commitments.

sampleQuestions.question: An agreement term is ending and the customer wants to continue. What should the team do?
options: Create an opportunity and repeat the entire sales cycle in every case
Renew the agreement for a new term
Extend the original agreement indefinitely
Leave the expired agreement active for future orders
sampleQuestions.explanation: A new agreement term can continue the relationship while preserving period-specific commitments.
whyWrong: An opportunity may be used in some renewal processes but is not always required.
Renewing the agreement creates a new term with updated commitments.
Leaving an expired agreement open can confuse future order and forecast tracking.
